concerns.text: The plan states that the numerical saddle‑point Meinardus asymptotic `Q_as_n` “contains no density terms” and that its calibration “does not involve any of the density predictors”. In fact, the saddle‑point evaluation uses the prime‑zeta function, which is itself a sum over primes and therefore encodes the prime‑density information (π(n), 1/ln n, cumulative reciprocal‑prime sum). Consequently the residual `R_n = log(p_P_n) - log(Q_as_n)` is not independent of the density predictors that will later be used in the regression. Modeling `R_n` with those same density features risks a circular validation: the predictors are already implicitly present in the baseline, so any observed association may be artefactual rather than evidence of a systematic correction term.
